newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Bacob seeking further Belgian acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Bacob seeking further Belgian acquisitions.

text.p: Belgian cooperative bank Bacob said on Friday it was looking for further acquisitions in Belgium.

Chief Executive Dirk Bruneel said that domestic acquisitions would be judged by three criteria -- whether they bring new customers, strengthen Bacob's distribution network or contribute any specialised knowledge.
"We have 12 to 15 billion francs available for further acquisitions but we do not feel limited by this amount," Bruneel said.
In August 1996 Bacob acquired 33 percent of Belgian agricultural bank Credit Agricole/Landbouwkrediet.

Earlier today it announced it bought a 75 percent stake in Belgian brokerage Smeets,Verbaet. The other 25 percent was bought buy Dutch Delta Lloyd bank, a unit of Dutch Delta Lloyd Insurance, itself a unit of British Commercial Union.
Bruneel reiterated that Bacob was still actively looking for a foreign partner but that no concrete talks were going on for the moment.
